title: Decision-Centric Large Deviations for Data-Driven Capital Buffers in Ruin Models
summary: We consider an insurance risk model with a random walk structure in which the underlying probability law is unknown. A decision maker observes a statistic $Q_n$ computed from $n$ historical observations and then needs to choose a capital buffer of the form $C_n=n f(c,Q_n)$, where $c=\log(1/δ)/n$ balances the amount of data and the tolerated ruin probability $δ$. The classical safe capital buffer is inversely proportional to the adjustment coefficient $γ$, the exponential rate at which the ruin probability decays; when the law is unknown, this coefficient must be inferred from the data.
